C1.implementedSubtask: Production original-rule ajax/connect now execute the finite original-FQN URL script stages before the existing single JVM HTTP transport; preserved original defaults, cancellation/deadline/owner boundaries and typed unsupported results.

URL stage order and original method semantics: @js/<js> with @result concatenation; original RuleAnalyzer string-delimiter innerRule {{JS}} overload; String/Double/null formatting; page alternative replacement including original negative/zero/out-of-range behavior. The original first end delimiter is retained, not replaced by a balanced JS parser.

URL JS uses the same Rhino engine and real Java AnalyzeUrl/Book/BookSource types, source inline library/CryptoJS, environment cookie/cache and owner-scoped handles. java.get/put retain chapter-before-ruleData precedence for the explicit finite URL model.

Nested ajax/connect use original defaults: only source and caller context plus explicit headers/timeout; key/page/ruleData/chapter are null, baseUrl is empty. Parent search/page/book input is not injected. Explicit key/page/model constructor tests are separate from those nested defaults.

The existing Rhino instruction observer has one optional ScriptExecutionGuard context element, whose only URL instance checks original task deadline/cancellation and environment lifetime. Guard-absent calls retain the previous coroutine cancellation check. Same real RuntimeTask Job; no Job inheritance, new timer, worker or alternate cancellation authority.

Original-rule SourceJavaHost qualification is private constructor state, default false for existing mainJs hosts. No script-visible internal/public bypass method or setter remains. Actual Rhino enumeration, attempted old mangled invocation and ordinary dynamic-connect rejection are verified.

URL boundary restores escaping typed UnsupportedRuleCapability/CancellationException only through up to 32 known ScriptException/WrappedException wrappers. JavaScript try/catch still catches host failures; ordinary script errors keep the previous ajax error-text policy. Exceptional exits recheck owner/caller/task so a closed owner cannot publish a stack body.

Vendor original-rule provenance now retains the exact original ZIP AnalyzeUrl bytes separately from finite ported bytes, refreshes modified port hashes, and records glue source hashes. Existing original ZIP entries/hashes and historical validation remain unchanged.
remaining: Finite URL-script phase, not full AnalyzeUrl constructor, analyzeUrl/getStrResponse orchestration, WebBook search/detail/TOC/content/pagination/batch, native JNI wiring or App reader route selection.

URL options js/bodyJs, source dynamic headers, browser/WebView, DNS/proxy/media, speech/extraParams/infoMap configuration, rate limiting and Android Room/WebView storage remain explicitly unported; existing finite allowed option checks reject unknown options before HTTP dispatch.

SourceJavaHost still prepares source/login headers after URL expansion, unlike upstream constructor initialization before initUrl. Login-site filtering uses the expanded resolved URL rather than original initial mUrl/baseUrl. Header option/replacement rules remain the existing finite transport contract, not full original header initialization parity.

Relative URL resolution still uses RuntimeSession.bookSourceUrl in SourceJavaHost. The nested URL JS baseUrl binding is the original empty default. Full original NetworkUtils resolution and baseUrl updates are not supplied by this expansion-only class.

RuleSource variables/login/cache are not yet unified with RuntimeSession stores. Cookie access shares the existing JVM in-memory URL/domain/path/scheme jar, not original registrable-domain Android Room/session/WebView persistence.

Environment close rejects future script instruction/host-return/publication boundaries, but does not interrupt arbitrary Java host code already running or cancel a shared task/session. The owned regression explicitly releases a held Java host after close.

Archive differential executes exactly two extracted original URL methods through a synthetic constructor/evaluator seam on Windows JVM. It does not execute Android or independently prove all Rhino binding/header/full constructor behavior. Separate explicit binding/type/loopback tests cover only their stated fixtures.
Windows JDK21 only; no Android/iOS/JNI/Zero/device execution, signing, install, auto-renewal, live websites or private user bookSource input.
